stories.title: The Morning the U.S. Bombed a School in Iran
stories.text: In the opening hours of the war against Iran, on February 28, 2026, the U.S. military fired Tomahawk cruise missiles directly at a school in the southern city of Minab. At least 156 people were killed that morning at Shajareh Tayyebeh school—120 of them were children and 26 were teachers. It will go down in history as one of the gravest war crimes committed by the U.S. government since Vietnam. Drop Site News conducted a two-month investigation into the strike, speaking with survivors, first responders, parents, doctors, teachers, psychologists, and other witnesses. stories.title: Germany Offered to Fund Their Education. It Won’t Help Them Leave Gaza.
stories.text: Photo: Ranin Al-Madhoun. This month, the winter semester begins at universities across Germany, and students will fill lecture halls as they begin their studies. Twenty-three-year-old Ranin Al-Madhoun will not be among them. She studied German intensively and won a competitive scholarship from the German Konrad Adenauer Foundation. But she is stuck in the Sheikh Radwan neighborhood of Gaza City. The scholarship, funded with public money, would pay her more than €1,000 a month to pursue a master’s degree in business administration at Niederrhein University of Applied Sciences in western Germany. But the German Embassy in Cairo, which handles visa applications from Gaza, requires applicants to appear in person—an impossible requirement for someone who cannot leave the Strip. “The first thing I imagine when I think about my life in Germany is a sense of safety,” she told Drop Site in an interview. “Things like going to the gym, studying, buying groceries, having a normal daily life.” She added: “We have had to flee six times during the war and live in a relative’s house because ours was destroyed.” On some days, her family can’t get drinking water. stories.title: Michigan Republican Tom Barrett Is Now Sour On Trump’s War in Iran—But Still Took Plenty of Defense Cash
stories.text: Rep. While Republican Rep. Tom Barrett has been actively working to distance himself from President Donald Trump and the administration’s unpopular war in Iran, defense industry PACs and executives have poured more than $58,000 into Republican Rep. Tom Barrett’s bid for reelection in Michigan’s 7th district. He has also been on the happy end of at least a million dollars in super PAC support from Trump. Barrett broke with Trump over the Iran war in May after he repeatedly voted to support the war. In April, he cast a tie-breaking vote to defeat a war powers resolution aimed at ending it. The measure failed 214-213. Of the nearly $60,000 Barrett has received directly from the defense industry, $38,000 has come from defense contractors like Oracle, Lockheed Martin, Booz Allen Hamilton and General Dynamics. The congressman notably received $10,000 from Oshkosh Corporation, a military vehicles and systems manufacturer, and $7,000 from SpaceX, Elon Musk’s aerospace giant, which provides the Department of War with missile tracking and launch services and satellite communications. stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: PopInfo Weekly: Hawks, Hawkeyes, and Hegseth
stories.text: Jay Feely, a former NFL kicker and CBS Sports analyst who is running for Congress in Arizona, has made “protecting women’s sports” a central theme of his campaign. Yet Feely has expressed retrograde views about female athletes. He described girls who compete in sports as “emotional” and more interested in getting along with their teammates than winning. Feely also argued that the WNBA is “the most unlikable league in the history of American sports.” President Trump’s super PAC, MAGA Inc., has raised over $400 million — more than any other entity has ever had to spend on the midterm elections. Trump raised a significant chunk of this unprecedented sum from corporations or individuals that are seeking, or recently received, favors from the Trump administration. On Tuesday, Trump unveiled a new website, America.gov, that he claims will be an interface that provides services from the federal government. Currently, America.gov functions as an AI chatbot that bases its answers on government data.
